perspective:
From Sara Manuelito’s subjective perspective, the information available to her is:

- She knows she is a Speech-Language Pathologist and an American Indian woman. She knows she and Shirley Whiteplume are long-time colleagues and close friends who have worked together at a community health center for several years. She knows Shirley is a nurse.
- At the funeral of a mutual patient, Sara observes Shirley looking somber and suspects Shirley is deeply affected by the loss.
- Sara tells Shirley that she knows this must be hard and that she saw how much Shirley cared. She hears Shirley say it has been tough and that Shirley keeps thinking something more could have been done. Sara replies that they did everything they could and should remember the good care and joy they brought into his life. Shirley says Sara is right, but it is hard to let go.
- During a coffee break at work, Sara raises the patient’s treatment decisions because she senses Shirley may feel burdened. Shirley says she feels responsible and wonders if pushing for a different approach might have given him a better chance. Sara says they made the best decisions with the information they had and that this burden is too heavy to carry alone. Shirley appreciates it but says it is hard to accept.
- After observing Shirley’s continued reserved behavior and minimal emotional expression, Sara confronts her in their office. Shirley says she is not sure she can open up and does not want to seem unprofessional or weak. Sara says showing emotions does not make someone weak and is healthy among friends. Shirley says maybe Sara is right and she will try to be more open.
- Sara later feels her previous confrontation may have been too harsh and apologizes. Shirley says it was a bit much but knows Sara meant well and appreciates the apology. Sara says she is there for Shirley however needed. Shirley thanks her and says they should keep talking because it helps.
- After some time, Sara notices improvements in Shirley’s demeanor and feels hopeful. She asks how Shirley is feeling. Shirley says she is feeling better thanks to their talks and Sara’s support. Sara suggests spending more time together outside work. Shirley agrees and says they can plan something for the weekend.

Sara does not have access to Shirley’s unspoken private thoughts or any events outside these interactions.
